Question: Which statement best describes a B cell receptor (BCR)?
Option A: A membrane-bound TCR that recognises antigen only when presented on MHC
Option B: A membrane-bound immunoglobulin (IgM) composed of two heavy and two light chains
Option C: A secreted antibody that circulates in mucosal surfaces
Option D: A receptor composed only of light chains that recognises peptides on MHC II
Correct Answer: A membrane-bound immunoglobulin (IgM) composed of two heavy and two light chains

Question: VDJ recombination during B cell development results in approximately how many different BCR combinations?
Which chromosomes encode the heavy and light chain loci for BCR gene rearrangement?
Option A: Heavy = chr 14; Light κ = chr 2; Light λ = chr 22
Option B: Heavy = chr 2; Light κ = chr 14; Light λ = chr 22
Option C: Heavy = chr 22; Light κ = chr 14; Light λ = chr 2
Option D: Heavy = chr 14; Light κ = chr 22; Light λ = chr 2
Correct Answer: Heavy = chr 14; Light κ = chr 2; Light λ = chr 22

Question: Which of the following is TRUE about how B cells recognise antigen compared with T cells?
Option A: Both B and T cells recognise free antigen in any form without MHC
Option B: B cells can recognise antigen in any biological form, whereas T cells require antigen presentation on MHC
Option C: B cells only recognise peptides on MHC II, while T cells recognise surface carbohydrates
Option D: Both require antigen to be presented on MHC I
Correct Answer: B cells can recognise antigen in any biological form, whereas T cells require antigen presentation on MHC

Question: Which event is sufficient by itself to generate low levels of IgM without T cell help?
Which pair of molecules/interactions is required to induce isotype switching?
Option B: CD40–CD40L interaction and cytokines from T helper cells
Option C: Complement activation and Fc receptor binding
Correct Answer: CD40–CD40L interaction and cytokines from T helper cells

Question: Affinity maturation primarily involves which mechanism?
Option A: Permanent change of the antibody constant region
Option B: Random mutations in the variable antigen-binding region producing higher-affinity antibodies on repeat exposure
Option C: Switching from IgM to IgG to increase affinity automatically
Correct Answer: Random mutations in the variable antigen-binding region producing higher-affinity antibodies on repeat exposure

Question: Which antibody effector function requires only the antigen-binding (Fab) region?
Option C: Pathogen neutralisation of microbes and toxins
Correct Answer: Pathogen neutralisation of microbes and toxins

Question: Which antibody class is the most abundant, can cross the placenta, and is involved in all antibody functions?
Which antibody class is secreted at mucosal surfaces and acquired via colostrum and milk?
Which effector mechanism involves NK cells recognising antibody-coated target cells via FcγRIII?
Which antibody class and cellular interaction are implicated in helminth expulsion and degranulation of mast cells/eosinophils?
Option C: IgE binding Fcε receptors on mast cells and eosinophils
Option D: IgA neutralising toxins at mucosal surfaces
Correct Answer: IgE binding Fcε receptors on mast cells and eosinophils
